title: Statement Cycle and Recent Postings — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Patient Statements
content:
Patient statements office — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program

# Statement cycle: postings not yet statemented

This note governs which postings not yet statemented come off the plan balance when the monthly installment of an interest-free payment plan on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment is priced.

**Rule.** The statement adjustment takes postings not yet statemented off the plan balance: when a remittance has posted on the program less than one whole calendar month before today, the program's recent remittances and recent patient charges come off, together with the insulin pump program's recent remittances and recent patient charges when it bills the same coverage record; when no remittance but a patient charge has posted less than one whole calendar month before today, only the recent patient charges of the program, and of the insulin pump program when it bills the same coverage record, come off; otherwise nothing comes off.

**Terms.**
- *The program* is the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment; *the insulin pump program* is the customer's Insulin Pump Program.
- *Recent postings* are those posted less than one whole calendar month before today. *Whole calendar months* from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day; a posting is recent when the whole calendar months from its posting date to today are 0.
- *A remittance* is a payer remittance posted on a program's billing ledger, its amount being the patient responsibility it leaves; *a patient charge* is a patient charge posted on that ledger.
- *Bills the same coverage record*: the Insulin Pump Program is not closed and its coverage record is the one the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment bills.
- Which case applies is decided by the postings on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment alone; a recent posting on the Insulin Pump Program does not by itself make anything come off. Recent Insulin Pump Program postings come off only when that program bills the same coverage record.

| Recent postings on the CGM enrollment | What comes off the plan balance |
|---|---|
| at least one recent remittance | the recent remittances and recent patient charges of the CGM enrollment, together with the recent remittances and recent patient charges of the Insulin Pump Program when it bills the same coverage record |
| no recent remittance, at least one recent patient charge | only the recent patient charges of the CGM enrollment, and of the Insulin Pump Program when it bills the same coverage record |
| neither | nothing |

**Boundary of "recent" (hypothetical dates).** Taking today as 15 June of a hypothetical year: a posting dated 16 May is 0 whole calendar months old (one calendar month apart, less one because the 15th is earlier than the 16th) and is recent; a posting dated 15 May is 1 whole calendar month old and is not recent; a posting dated 15 June is recent.

**Hypothetical case.** On the CGM enrollment a remittance leaving 83.40 of patient responsibility posted on 2 June and a patient charge of 46.15 on 10 June; on the customer's active Insulin Pump Program, which bills the same coverage record, a remittance leaving 31.70 posted on 4 June and a patient charge of 27.35 on 12 June. Taking today as 15 June, 83.40 and 46.15 come off for the CGM enrollment, and 31.70 and 27.35 for the Insulin Pump Program. Had the Insulin Pump Program billed another coverage record, only 83.40 and 46.15 would come off. Had only the 46.15 charge posted recently on the CGM enrollment, only the recent patient charges — 46.15 and, the pump billing the same coverage record, 27.35 — would come off. Had nothing posted recently on the CGM enrollment, nothing would come off, the recent Insulin Pump Program postings included.
